headline: Five days without a run — the taper's quiet stretch has held longer than any gap this block. Legs are rested, the engine is banked. Twelve days to the crossing.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The running side has gone fully quiet since the sharp tempo, and that's the correct read this close to departure — no drift back toward intensity, no restless filler miles. The recent four-week block was a genuine build before this wind-down, so the current stillness sits on top of real accumulated volume rather than masking a gap. Strength has also gone silent for several days, which matters more than the running quiet: the prior weeks kept it short and maintenance-level, exactly as intended, and the last logged sessions were low-HR and controlled. Steps remain high on training-adjacent days, so the background load hasn't collapsed even as structured work pauses — the bike commute and daily movement are carrying the baseline. Sleep is patchy and the cardio-load status reads as detraining, but both are supporting signals only, and the detraining flag here is a mechanical artefact of a deliberate taper, not a fitness verdict.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a clear build followed by an intentional descent — the recent four weeks stepped up meaningfully over the prior four, then folded into taper right on schedule for the event window. Year-to-date, the distance gap over last year is enormous, which frames this taper correctly: it's a pause at a high plateau, not a retreat to a low one. The shape makes sense against the standing goal of durable year-round capacity with a near-term crossing to be fresh for. Nothing here suggests plateau or irregularity — it's a well-formed peak-and-ease.
sections.threshold: The threshold figure is still anchored to a single early-July test with no rolling baseline yet, so read it as a reference point rather than a live trend. What's more informative right now is the behaviour of easy-run HR through the build — controlled at genuinely easy paces — which tells you the aerobic engine is intact and efficient. That's the quality that carries a multi-day self-supported effort, and it's demonstrably in place. No reason to expect it has eroded in a few quiet days.
sections.zones: Across the block the distribution has been appropriately easy-skewed, with most sessions sitting in Z1–Z2 and only the deliberate tempo pushing into Z4. That last hard run was a true mixed effort — real time up in Z3 and Z4 rather than a flat grind at a middling average — which is exactly what a single sharpening stimulus should look like before a taper. The surrounding runs stayed clean in the easy band with minimal grey-zone bleed. For a block whose job is to arrive fresh with the engine primed, that's the right shape: one quality touch, everything else controlled.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions have run low and steady in the aerobic sense — consistent with short maintenance work rather than metabolically demanding circuits — and the estimated HR sits comfortably where you'd expect for that intent. The one run that lacked chest-strap data slotted in line with its neighbours, so source agreement isn't raising any flags. Nothing here worth acting on.
sections.calendar: The rhythm through the build was reliably rota-like — a few runs a week interleaved with regular strength — which is why the current cluster of empty days stands out against the athlete's own pattern rather than blending in. This isn't the erratic on-off of lost consistency; it's a clean, uniform pause after a dense stretch. The contrast itself is the signal that the taper is real and intentional.
sections.personal_bests: None of the standing PBs are in play during a taper, and chasing one now would work directly against the point of the next twelve days. The speed bests sit from a sharper period last autumn; the ultra/distance side is where current focus lives, and the crossing is a durability event, not a PB attempt. Nothing to pursue here right now.

watch_items: Watch that the first run back lands squarely in the easy band and feels unremarkable, confirming the tempo left no residue.
Watch whether the strength pause resumes as brief maintenance or stays dark through to departure — either is fine, but note which.
Watch that daily movement and steps hold their baseline through the pause so the legs stay ticking over rather than going fully cold.
Watch how sleep tracks as travel logistics ramp — observe it, don't let it drive anything.
